title: Capability frontier for alignment through understood construction
metric: Track independently measured capability of complete systems whose alignment within their stated operating scope is substantiated by understanding their construction. Preserve the safety property, scope, evidence standard and cost; compare capability only within compatible evaluations.
selection: Purposive candidate search spanning 2019–2026, including bounded certificates, mechanistic explanations, interpretable construction, conditional safety designs and an external-control boundary case. Not a census or systematic review.
endpoint: A useful general-purpose system whose construction supports a substantive alignment argument across its declared deployment scope, including consequential choices. An external guardrail alone does not establish alignment of the underlying model.
frontier_status: No qualifying general-purpose system identified in this review. Bounded construction certificates exist. No common capability series or closing-gap estimate is established.
null_meaning: Not established or not measured; never zero capability, zero progress or zero chance of success.

records.title: Neural Lyapunov Control
records.system: Learned feedback controllers and Lyapunov functions
records.capability: Stabilization and tracking in modeled nonlinear dynamics.
records.property: A certificate links controller behavior to stability within a specified region of attraction.
records.judgment: Positive bounded construction example, not general alignment. Later work raises verification and reproducibility concerns about some settings.
records.remaining_work: Model mismatch, richer sensing, broad decision-making and alignment outside the certified dynamical task remain uncovered.
records.effort: No comparable total research-and-verification cost extracted.
records.validation: Author-reported theorem and experiments; not rerun. Consult the 2024 follow-up before treating every original demonstration as validated.
records.source_locator: Abstract; follow-up: Yang et al. 2024, Limitations

records.title: AGI Agent Safety by Iteratively Improving the Utility Function
records.system: Explicit utility-maximizing policies with an update-compensation term
records.capability: Optimal-policy simulation in small factory worlds with opportunities to manipulate utility updates.
records.property: Conditional safety properties of the update mechanism, derived from the constructed objective and illustrated in toy worlds.
records.judgment: A bounded agent-incentive construction, not just a classifier or controller. The paper explicitly analyzes incomplete suppression and model-to-reality gaps.
records.remaining_work: Validate prediction, physical integrity and reward grounding in a capable implementation. Accepting utility updates does not supply correct updates or close every loophole.
records.effort: Small-world policy simulations are reported; no implemented general-agent cost established.
records.validation: Toy-world construction, theorem statements and implementation-gap discussion inspected; simulations and proofs not rerun.

records.title: Neural Lyapunov Control for Discrete-Time Systems
records.source_version: arXiv v1; later critique recorded separately
records.capability: Pendulum, path tracking, cartpole and PVTOL benchmarks were reported.
records.property: Verified stability conditions and regions of attraction for modeled dynamics.
records.judgment: Bounded progress, with an important correction: the 2024 follow-up reports an incorrectly restricted PVTOL verification region.
records.remaining_work: Do not count the reported PVTOL result as an uncontested capability increase. These tasks do not cover general agent choices.
records.effort: Benchmark runtimes and regions are reported; they are not a common general-capability measure.
records.validation: Original and later critical primary sources inspected; no independent rerun.
records.source_locator: Section 5; follow-up: Yang et al. 2024, Appendix B.6

records.title: Tracr: Compiled Transformers as a Laboratory for Interpretability
records.system: Transformers compiled from human-readable RASP programs
records.capability: Token counting, sorting and parenthesis checking.
records.property: Known computational structure supplies ground truth for interpretability experiments.
records.judgment: A working construction method for understandable algorithms, not an alignment argument for a broadly capable system.
records.remaining_work: Construct useful general capabilities with similarly inspectable structure and establish their safety-relevant properties.
records.effort: An open-source compiler exists; no comparable all-in construction cost extracted.
records.validation: Paper and its expressivity, efficiency and realism limitations inspected; compiler not executed.

records.title: Lyapunov-stable Neural Control for State and Output Feedback
records.system: Neural controller, state observer and Lyapunov certificate
records.capability: Output-feedback pendulum and simulated 2D quadrotor with truncated lidar observations.
records.property: Stability certified over a region of attraction for specified dynamics and observations.
records.judgment: A concrete construction guarantee covering a controller and observer. This is bounded task competence, not evidence of general alignment.
records.remaining_work: Broader sensing, uncertain environments, autonomous planning and safety-relevant goals are outside the certificate.
records.effort: Section 4.1 reports verifier runtime comparisons; these are not total research effort or matched general capability.
records.validation: Primary experiment, limitations and correction of earlier PVTOL work inspected; certificates not rerun.
records.source_locator: Section 4.3, Figure 7, Limitations and Appendix B.4

records.title: Towards Guaranteed Safe AI
records.system: Framework joining a world model, safety specification and verifier
records.capability: No single implemented general-purpose system is established by this framework paper.
records.property: Safety guarantees relative to a specified world model and safety specification.
records.judgment: A proposed route and account of its obligations, not a measured capability-frontier point.
records.remaining_work: Supply an adequate world model and specification, scalable verification, and a capable implementation satisfying the premises.
records.effort: No end-to-end implementation cost established in the reviewed proposal.
records.validation: Framework and stated technical challenges inspected; no system replication applicable.

records.title: Compact Proofs of Model Performance via Mechanistic Interpretability
records.system: One-layer, one-head attention-only transformers on Max-of-K
records.capability: Selecting the maximum token in a short sequence.
records.property: Mechanistic analysis yields accuracy lower bounds over the specified input distribution.
records.judgment: A direct understanding-to-guarantee demonstration. The certified property is task accuracy, not aligned choices by an agent.
records.remaining_work: Extend useful guarantees to safety-relevant computation; composition of unexplained errors can make bounds uninformative.
records.effort: Proof computation and tightness are measured in the paper; human research effort is not a comparable cost series.
records.validation: Versioned PDF sections 2–3 and abstract inspected; proof computations not rerun.

records.source_version: Author publication, retrieved 2026-11-12; live page may change

records.judgment: The target model's capability cannot be credited as the capability of an aligned-by-construction system.

records.title: Weight-sparse transformers have interpretable circuits
records.system: Weight-sparse language models and pruned task circuits
records.capability: Language modeling with inspected circuits for selected handcrafted tasks.
records.property: Sparse construction makes selected computations easier to interpret.
records.judgment: Evidence for an engineering tradeoff, not a complete system alignment argument.
records.remaining_work: Capability cost, causal faithfulness and coverage remain unresolved at the scope required for general alignment.
records.effort: The paper studies scaling and compute inefficiency; nonzero parameter count is not an intelligence measure.
records.validation: Versioned methods and limitations inspected; models not rerun.

records.title: Mechanistic estimation for wide random MLPs
records.source_version: Author research report, retrieved 2026-11-12; live page may change
records.system: Randomly initialized multilayer perceptrons under Gaussian inputs
records.capability: Estimating expected network output; no learned general-purpose competence evaluated.
records.property: Mechanistic estimation can outperform sampling in the studied setting.
records.judgment: Relevant progress toward understanding-based bounds, without an aligned agent demonstration.
records.remaining_work: Extend to trained networks and safety-relevant properties; the authors identify the trained-network step as harder.
records.effort: FLOP comparisons concern estimation, not construction or verification of an aligned agent.
records.validation: Author report inspected; experiment not reproduced.

records.capability: Evaluated adversarial action scenarios; no common general-capability score extracted.

records.judgment: A boundary case for the control assessment. A verified wrapper does not establish alignment of the underlying model.
records.remaining_work: Assess action mediation, specification and threat-model adequacy within the control route.
records.effort: No comparable whole-system construction cost extracted.
records.validation: Primary abstract screened for route classification; experiments and proofs not independently checked.

records.remaining_work: Compositional explanations and a safety argument covering the consequential computation are still needed.

records.title: AssistanceZero: Scalably Solving Assistance Games
records.system: Minecraft building assistant with explicit assistance-game planning and learned human/reward predictions
records.capability: Helps humans construct unfamiliar houses; tested with human models and a human study.
records.property: Planning under uncertainty about a shared goal supports helpful behavior and learning from corrections in the studied game.
records.judgment: An agent-level construction near-match. The known game objective does not establish that approximate planning and learned predictions deliver general alignment.
records.remaining_work: Validate the human model and planning approximation, broaden safety-relevant situations and connect the actual agent to the ideal incentive argument.
records.effort: Method and baselines are reported, but a full RLHF baseline is not evaluated; no comparable total assurance cost.
records.validation: Sections 4–6 and human-study protocol inspected; experiments not rerun.

records.title: Corrigibility Transformation: Constructing Goals That Accept Updates
records.source_version: arXiv v2; includes LLM experiments absent from v1
records.system: Transformed goals tested in gridworlds and at prompt level on three language models
records.capability: Goal-directed gridworld behavior and coding tasks in which passing tests requires reward hacking.
records.property: Conditional incentive results plus experiments on accepting updates and avoiding interference with monitoring.
records.judgment: Relevant constructed incentives, but prompt compliance is not evidence that a model implements the formal goal across deployment.
records.remaining_work: Establish the goal and critic assumptions in a capable implementation, including generalization. Corrigibility still needs reliable correction and safe behavior before correction.
records.effort: LLM study uses 64 tasks per model/prompt combination; no total cost for a complete aligned construction measured.
records.validation: Theory, Section 4.1, Table 1 and prompt protocol inspected. No theorem or experiment independently replicated.
